It is Meccan in its entirety, by consensus.

The first: that it is the term of death; this was said by Mujahid. The meaning then: indeed the term of Allah by which He has deferred you to it will not be postponed when it comes, so faith will not be possible for you at that time.

The second: that it is the term of resurrection; this was said by al-Hasan.

The third: that it is the term of punishment; this was said by al-Suddi and Muqatil.

(p-٣٧١) **Allah's words: "What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?"** (71:13). There are four opinions about this.

The first is that you do not see greatness in Allah. This was said by al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

The second is that you do not fear the greatness of Allah. This was also said by al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba.

The third is that you do not see obedience to Allah as anything. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth is that you do not hope for the outcome of faith and monotheism. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

**"And He has created you in stages"** (71:14). That is, He has placed in yourselves a sign that points to His oneness, in that He created you from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, one thing after another, until the end of creation. Ibn al-Anbari said: *al-tawr* (stage) means a state, and its plural is *atwar*. Ibn Faris said: *al-tawr* means a turn, "a stage after a stage," that is, one time after another. It was also said that by *atwar* is meant the variation in appearances and characters, such as tall and short and other differences. Then He established the matter for them, saying: **"Have you not seen how Allah created seven heavens in layers?"** (71:15). Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi 'Abla recited *tibaqin* with the *qaf* nunated and vocalized with a kasra, without an alif. We have explained this in the commentary on Surah al-Mulk (67:3).

**"And He made the moon within them a light"** (71:16). There are two opinions about this.

One is that the face of the moon is toward the heavens and its back toward the earth, shining for the people of the heavens as it shines for the people of the earth. Likewise the sun. This is the statement of Abd Allah ibn Amr.

The second is that the moon is in the lowest heaven. He said "within them" because they are like one thing, as mentioned by al-Akhfash, al-Zajjaj and others. This is like your saying: "I came to the Banu Tamim," when you only came to some of them, and "I rode the ships." **"And He made the sun a lamp"** (71:16), by which the world is illuminated.

**"And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth"** (71:17). That is, the beginning of your creation was from the earth, namely Adam, **"a growth"** (71:17). Al-Khalil said: its meaning is "so you grew a growth." Al-Zajjaj said: *nabatan* (a growth) is a verbal noun governed by the meaning, since the meaning of "He caused you to grow" is "He made you grow a growth." Ibn Qutayba said: this is one of the cases where the verbal noun comes not in the form of the verb, because it came from *nabata*. Similar to it is **"and devote yourself to Him with a devotion"** (73:8), which came in the form of *battala* (not *tabattala*).

The poet said:
"The best of affairs is what you encounter of it, and it is not to follow it with following."
Here it came in the form of *ittaba'tu*.

Another said:
"And if you wish, we shall return to our repetition."
Here it came in the form of *'awadna*. Verbal nouns come differing from the verbs, because verbs, though their patterns differ, are one in meaning.

**"Broad roads"** (71:20). Al-Farra' said: these are wide paths.

**"And they followed one whose wealth and children did not increase him"** (71:21). The people of Medina, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim recited *wa-waladuhu* with a fatha on the lam and the waw. The rest recited *wulduhu* with a damma on the waw and a sukun on the lam. Al-Zajjaj said: both have the same meaning, like *al-'arab* and *al-'urb*, and *al-'ajam* and *al-'ujm*. Al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliya, Ibn Ya'mar and al-Jahdari recited *wiluduhu* with a kasra on the waw and a sukun on the lam. The commentators said: the meaning is that the followers and the poor followed the opinion of the leaders and the great ones.

**"And they schemed a great scheme"** (71:22). Abu Raja' and Abu 'Imran recited *kubaran* with a damma on the kaf and a light ba'. Ibn Ya'mar, Abu al-Jawza' and Ibn Muhaysin recited *kibaran* with a kasra on the kaf and a light ba'. The meaning is *kabiran* (great). It is said *kabir* and *kubar*. We have explained this at the beginning of Surah Sad (38). The meaning of "scheme" is striving in corruption. This is because the leaders prevented their followers from believing in Nuh.

**"And they said: Do not abandon your gods"** (71:23), that is, do not leave off worshipping them. **"Nor abandon Wadd"** (71:23). Abu Ja'far and Nafi' recited it with a damma on the waw. The rest recited it with a fatha. This name and what follows are the names of their gods. It has come in the commentary that these are the names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Nuh. A people arose after them who took up their worship, and Iblis said to them: "If you made their images, it would be more energizing for you and more eager for worship." They did so. Then another people arose after them, and Iblis said to them: "Those who came before you used to worship them," so they worshipped them. The beginning of idol worship was from that time. Those images were named by these names because they fashioned them after the forms of those people named by these names. It was also said: these are names of the children of Adam. One of them died, and Satan came and said: "Shall I make for you his likeness, so that you remember him by it?" So he made it. Then another died, and he made their likeness for them, until he had made five images. Then time lengthened, and they abandoned the worship of Allah. Satan said to them: "What is the matter with you that you do not worship anything?" They said: "Whom should we worship?" He said: "These are your gods and the gods of your fathers. Do you not see them pictured in your places of prayer?" So they worshipped them.

Al-Zajjaj said: these idols belonged to the people of Nuh, then they passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to the Kalb, Suwa' to Hamdan, and Yaghuth to the Banu Ghutayf, who were a tribe of Murad. The rest recited it with a fatha. This name and what follows are the names of their gods. It has come in the commentary that these are the names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Nuh. A people arose after them who took up their worship, and Iblis said to them: "If you made their images, it would be more energizing for you and more eager for worship." They did so. Then another people arose after them, and Iblis said to them: "Those who came before you used to worship them," so they worshipped them. The beginning of idol worship was from that time. Those images were named by these names because they fashioned them after the forms of those people named by these names. It was also said: these are names of the children of Adam. One of them died, and Satan came and said: "Shall I make for you his likeness, so that you remember him by it?" So he made it. Then another died, and he made their likeness for them, until he had made five images. Then time lengthened, and they abandoned the worship of Allah. Satan said to them: "What is the matter with you that you do not worship anything?" They said: "Whom should we worship?" He said: "These are your gods and the gods of your fathers. Do you not see them pictured in your places of prayer?" So they worshipped them.

Al-Zajjaj said: these idols belonged to the people of Nuh, then they passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to the Kalb, Suwa' to Hamdan, and Yaghuth to the Banu Ghutayf, who were a tribe of Murad. It was also said: when the Flood came, it covered these idols and the dust buried them. When they appeared after the Flood, they passed to those mentioned. Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of an eagle among birds.

**"And they have led many astray"** (71:24). There are two opinions about this.

One is that the idols have led many people astray, that is, they went astray because of them.

The second is that the great ones have led many people astray. **"And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error"** (71:24), meaning the disbelievers. This is a supplication by Nuh against them, after Allah informed him that they would not believe.
